text: Topic: how to judge graph vs graph+harness (step 2). User's view: problems that represent several axes, judged comprehensively, strengths and weaknesses per axis.
Rigor first: blind arms, judge on another tier, enough runs to beat noise, axes defined before results.
Every axis must be measurable cheaply and repeatably; tokens, wall time, flake rate, Codex availability.
Judge what teams will inherit: the axes teams users feel (verified output, recoveries, visibility), not engine internals.
A: Axis-matrix blind bench. 5 axes x 3 problems x 3 runs per arm, Codex off for both, anonymized, Opus judge vs pre-registered per-axis rubric, per-axis win/tie/loss with variance bands.
B: Seeded-defect bench. Planted flaws so scoring is mechanical: detection rate, false-pass rate, cost, time; 2 clean controls; judge only for report honesty.
C: Two-tier staged bench. 1-run pilot per axis to find gaps, replicate only those at n=5 with blind pairwise judging; Codex axis replayed after auth is fixed.
A: Offline deterministic bench. Fixed fixtures through both arms' engines, no LLM/Codex: gate correctness, now.json, severity, fallback paths. ~$0-2, 3h, zero flake.
B: Stage-truncated live A/B. 6 small problems, 1 per axis, run only to the stage the axis touches, 3 repeats, opus blind judge. ~$60-90, 8h.
C: Tiered funnel. Offline first, live only where it shows a gap, one size-S canary per arm, hard stop $50; Codex marked unmeasured.
A: Failure-replay bench. Replay the four real teams failures on both arms; judge accepted work kept, cost to resolve, whether the person is told.
B: Four-axis matrix: verified output, recovery, progress visibility, decision surfacing; 2 problems each, blind, per-axis strengths/weaknesses.
C: Person-in-the-loop trace audit. One medium task with injected faults; a reviewer reads only the artifacts and answers what is happening/decided/left, checked against the repo.
Axis-matrix blind bench (methodologist A + PO B): pre-registered axes, problems per axis, repeats, blind judge, per-axis win/tie/loss
Seeded-defect and failure-replay bench (methodologist B + PO A): planted flaws plus the four real teams failures, mechanical scoring
Offline deterministic bench (cost A): recorded fixtures, no model calls, engine behaviour only
Tiered funnel (methodologist C + cost C): cheap screen, replicate only axes with a gap, size-S canary, cost cap
Person-in-the-loop trace audit (PO C): artifacts-only reviewer judges visibility, decisions and report truth
Only O1 matches the multi-axis view: pre-registered axes, blind, Opus judge, variance bands. Add a stated minimum effect size so ties are not misread as wins.
Fixtures test the author's own model of failure: the engine does what it was coded to do, not that it helps. A smoke gate, not the verdict; cannot cover judgment axes.
A 1-run pilot screen is mostly noise: real gaps dropped, noise replicated; dropped axes lose their strengths/weaknesses.
Best-instrumented (mechanical scoring, controls, false-pass rate) but planted defects are not the real distribution: use it as the verification axis inside O1.
n=1 and unblindable (artifact layout reveals the arm). Use for the visibility axis only, two reviewers, claims checked.
User's view survives with one amendment: never sum axes into one score; adoption into teams is decided per axis.
axes x problems x repeats x 2 arms is 100+ runs, several hundred dollars, one-shot and unrepeatable.
$0, zero flake, runs every commit, Codex irrelevant; covers engine behaviour where graph and harness differ. Base layer.
Only option with a spend ceiling; bounds the $60-built-nothing failure by design.
Unrepeatable reader; keep as one end check on report truth, never a gate.
Cheap only if the four teams failures replay offline; fold replays into O3 fixtures, drop live seeding.
User's view survives with a cost-and-flake budget per axis; axes not measurable cheaply reported unmeasured, not scored.
Engine checks say nothing about whether accepted work survives a failure or whether the person is told. Cheap but the wrong question.
Random problems seldom trigger recovery or decision surfacing; per-axis tie then means untested.
The four real teams failures are what teams inherits; planted defects make false-pass mechanical.
Only option that tests visibility directly; answers checked against the repo keep it honest.
An offline-first screen never lets visibility/surfacing axes reach the live tier; seed it with O2 and O5 cases.
User's view survives if axes come from teams user pain and are exercised by injected faults; an unseeded equal-weight matrix does not.
Cut as a standalone verdict: does not solve the stated problem (no judgment/visibility axes). Kept as the base layer of F1.
Cut as standalone: n=1, unblindable, unrepeatable. Kept as the visibility-axis instrument (two reviewers, claims checked).
Unseeded full matrix cut: unbounded cost (100+ runs) and rare failures stay untested. Its rules survive: pre-registered axes, blind, per-axis verdict, no total.

Finalists: F1 layered (O3 base + O2 seeded/replayed faults on every axis + O5 visibility, O1 rules, $ cap, no pilot dropping axes); F2 seeded matrix (O1 with fault-injected problems from teams pain, fixed n, no funnel).
User chose F2 (seeded matrix, repeated runs): "여러 번 돌려보는게 맞을거 같음".
